title: Agility 57–99 · Hardcore Worlds edition
subtitle: Zerker build with quest-only Defence · informed danger: every risk shown, every risk prepared for
intro:
Welcome to the rooftops, adventurer. This guide takes your Hardcore Worlds character from where your Agility stands today to the cape at the top, and it is written as an expedition briefing, not a lecture. You have one life, and on Hardcore Worlds almost every death counts, including many that are safe for a Hardcore Ironman. So every step tells you plainly what can kill you, why the step is still worth doing, and exactly how to prepare. You asked to be informed, not shielded: nothing here is hidden because it is dangerous, and every choice stays yours.

Reading the danger badge: the big number is the headline score, the danger with no precautions at all. It sits on the same game-wide ladder as every other activity, with The Fractured Archive at the very top of the scale, so a quest fight here can be compared like for like with a boss or a raid. The small 'with prep' number is what the step's prep card buys you when you follow every mandatory line of it. From a High headline upward, the full prep card is printed with the step: mitigations, minimum Hitpoints, stop conditions, bail-out plan and why the step is worth it. The ladder also carries a tiered Wilderness premium that grows with depth, but no step in this guide sets foot in the Wilderness, so it adds nothing here.

Two routes. Safest uses only the low-danger quests and the rooftops (Falador, Seers', Pollnivneach, Ardougne). Balanced adds the quest block you can reach today (Icthlarin's Little Helper, A Tail of Two Cats, Underground Pass, Regicide, The Fremennik Trials) and swaps Pollnivneach for Rellekka before Ardougne. Two honest notes from the Quant. First, route totals are training hours only: they exclude all quest time, because no verified source gives quest durations. Second, do not read Balanced as faster than Safest. Most of the gap between their totals comes from training on Rellekka instead of Pollnivneach, and the quests are counted as taking no time at all; if the quest block takes longer than the little Falador training it replaces, it costs time rather than saving it. Choose Balanced for what its quests give you (the lyre to Rellekka, Tirannwn, and the quest Defence your zerker plan wants), not for speed.

Standing rules for every step: Defence comes only from quests, never from a lamp, a tome or a combat style; on Ranged use Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange. Dismiss every random event (a death inside one is official), never go AFK on a course, never use a player-owned house, Nightmare Zone or the Rogues' Den maze, never drink a poison chalice for a boost, and never step into the Wilderness. Where a decision point offers a choice, the options, their danger and the recommendation travel with you in the 'What next?' panel.

steps.summary: Danger first: this quest is under a month old and its prison cell blocks teleports, so read today's walkthrough before you start. In return it gives {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP, no required kills and no Defence XP.
instructions: Before anything else, open the current wiki walkthrough and read it end to end. If it now lists any fight, aggressive monster or damage source not described on this card, stop and ask for a re-rating.
Bank: withdraw the mid-heal food listed on the card and one teleport you can use outside the prison cell.
Gear: your normal non-Defence setup; the quest needs no combat.
Travel: start with Betty at Land's End, at full HP.
Do: follow the quest. The ambush is a scripted knock-out cutscene, not a fight.
Do: in the Port Piscarilius prison cell, do not try to teleport. Remove the plank, climb out through the gap in the north wall and walk clear of the guards before you teleport.
Stop: when the quest completes. The Thieving reward also moves you toward Death on the Isle's Thieving requirement.
warnings: Mandatory: re-read the walkthrough on the day you start. This is new content, the page is still being edited and its two dungeons were not reviewed for aggressive monsters. Anything new on the page means stop and get a re-rating first.
Mandatory: start at full HP with the card's food and a teleport, and never enter the prison area below {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP.
The prison cell is teleport-blocked and a guard who catches you sends you back into it. The only way out is the plank and the north-wall gap.
Stop condition: if you are losing HP in a dungeon and cannot see why, leave the dungeon at once (the exact HP line is in 'Stop immediately if').
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
Any death here is official and run-ending: no Hardcore Worlds safe exception covers this quest.
tips: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}): the score is held up by the new-content floor, not by any known damage. The walkthrough re-read is what the card asks of you.

steps.summary: A short Kourend quest for {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP; the only kill is a weak Sand Snake you can safespot.
instructions: Bank: a bow and arrows for the safespot, the few mid-heal food listed on the card, and a teleport.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: Great Kourend. The Crabclaw Caves section is an instance.
Do: be at full HP before every stepping stone and rock, and eat back to full after any fall.
Do: fight the Sand Snake only from the west-wall safespot: go north or south along the west wall, then hug it back to the centre entrance.
Stop: when the quest completes. To leave the caves early, walk out the way you came and teleport once you are outside the instance.
warnings: Mandatory: fight the snake only from the west-wall safespot with Ranged. Stop condition: if the safespot does not hold and the snake reaches you, leave the cave.
Mandatory: full HP with food before crossing the stepping stones and rocks; their fall damage is not published.
Stop condition: stop and eat if HP falls to the card's eat line.
Do not count on a teleport inside the cave: whether it works there is not stated. Walk out first.
tips: Its prerequisites are already done, and fixed XP is worth most here, where training is slowest.

steps.summary: {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP and the key to A Tail of Two Cats' lamps. What can kill you is a fight inside a teleport-blocked flashback; the right protection prayer, held throughout, is what makes it safe to do.
instructions: Bank: the card's food, full waterskins, an antipoison, prayer restores, your cat or kitten, and Ranged gear.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: magic carpet across the desert with full waterskins. Never walk the River Elid banks or the area north of Sophanem.
Do: examine the canopic jar before the pit jump; it sets which guardian you will face.
Do: turn on the right prayer before each fight and hold it to the end, starting with full prayer: Protect from Magic for the Possessed Priest and for Apmeken, Protect from Melee for Het or Scabaras.
Do: in Klenter's Pyramid, cure scarab poison at once with your antipoison.
Stop: when the quest completes, then go straight on to A Tail of Two Cats while the cat and desert travel are fresh.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Once a flashback starts you cannot teleport until it ends; a disconnect in there with no prayer up is what kills. The guardian facts say the correct protection prayer protects fully, and that is the whole prep card in one line.

Mandatory: enter each flashback at full HP and full prayer with food. If prayer or HP falls to the card's lines, walk back toward the entrance, or log out once you have gone long enough without being hit.
Stop conditions: do not start a flashback with prayer under the card's line; leave the flashback if HP falls to the card's line; never start the pit jump without having examined the jar.
Mandatory: desert travel only by carpet with waterskins. The River Elid and the area north of Sophanem mean heat and aggressive crocodiles.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
A death here is official on Hardcore Worlds, and it also loses your cat.
tips: Why it is worth it: the Agility XP plus the gate to A Tail of Two Cats and its two lamps. Safer choice: decision point `DP02` option A skips this whole block.

steps.summary: No required kills: rub both lamps into Agility for {{step.xp_gained}} XP.
instructions: Bank: death runes, a chocolate cake (buy it rather than cooking it), your cat or kitten, a few food and full waterskins (exact counts on the card).
Gear: light travel gear; no fight is required.
Travel: magic carpet across the desert. Never walk the river banks or north of Sophanem.
Do: follow the quest; the dragon scenes are cutscenes.
Do: rub both lamps and choose Agility. Never Defence.
Stop: when both lamps are spent and the quest is complete.
warnings: Mandatory: both lamps go into Agility (or another non-Defence skill). Never click Defence.
Mandatory: carpet-only desert travel with full waterskins. Stop condition: leave the desert if your waterskins run out.
Stop condition: if any part of the quest asks for a fight not described here, stop and ask for a re-rating.

steps.summary: {{step.xp_gained}} fixed Agility XP and the only door to Regicide. What can kill you: failed bridge jumps that drop you among aggressive Soulless, spider pile-ups after Kalrag, and Iban's temple spikes that ignore prayer. Every required fight can be safespotted.
instructions: Bank: a large stack of food (the card gives the minimum; there is no bank beyond the Pass), prayer restores, an instant teleport, a bow with the non-poisoned metal-tipped arrows the quest needs, and Ranged ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: West Ardougne to the Pass entrance. The whole quest is an instance, and any instant teleport gets you out.
Do: be at {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP or more before every Iban's Lair bridge jump, the rope swing and the Kalrag fight, and eat as soon as you reach the card's eat line.
Do: safespot the demons from the narrow pathways and the paladins by attacking and running west, with Ranged. Keep Protect from Melee on for Kalrag.
Do: use the plank on wall traps and never stand in front of an armed trap. When Kalrag dies you are briefly stunned; then leave the spider corridor at once.
Do: enter Iban's temple only at full HP and run in without stopping. If the spikes stun you back to the entrance, step back, eat to full, and only then try again.
Stop: when the quest completes, or teleport out the moment a stop condition below is met.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Why it is still worth it: it is the gate to Regicide, the largest Agility reward you can reach today, and much later to the elf chain toward Prifddinas.
Mandatory: never jump a bridge or take the rope swing below {{risk.min_hitpoints}} HP. A failed jump hits hard against your HP and lands you among aggressive Soulless.
Mandatory: Protect from Melee does NOTHING against the spikes at Iban's temple. Enter only at full HP and never retry hurt: after any spike stun, eat back to full first.
Stop condition: if the spikes stun you back to the entrance twice in a row, or your food is below the card's temple reserve, teleport out and restock.

Stop conditions: teleport out if HP falls to the card's line with no food left, or if more than three monsters are attacking you at once. If stunned among spiders after Kalrag, eat first, then teleport.
Never stand in front of an armed wall trap: the wiki warns it can hit repeatedly and fast enough to kill.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: The owner accepted this step's earlier card on the record; under the informed policy no new acceptance is needed, but read the current card before you go.

steps.summary: The largest Agility reward you can reach today, {{step.xp_gained}} fixed XP, and the key to Tirannwn. The danger is the Tyras guard ambush in the forest and a second trip through the Underground Pass with no bank beyond it.
instructions: Bank: the card's food, an antipoison, prayer restores, an instant teleport, and Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: back through the Underground Pass, under every Underground Pass rule: bridges and the rope swing only at the card's HP line or above.
Do: turn Protect from Melee on before climbing through the dense forest. Keep it on until you are in the mushroom safespot or the guard is dead, then finish him from the safespot with Ranged.
Do: watch for Isafdar trap tiles and step around them; cure tripwire poison at once.
Do: once you hold the Big Book of Bangs, the coal tar and the sulphur, leave Isafdar by teleport rather than on foot.
Stop: when the quest completes.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). A disconnect as the Tyras guard engages is the killer; Protect from Melee, documented to stop this guard, is what removes it.
Mandatory: never climb through the dense forest with prayer under the card's line.
Mandatory: never jump a Pass bridge below the card's HP line. Stop condition: teleport out if HP falls to the card's line and your food is gone.
Bail-out: if the guard is hitting you, keep Protect from Melee on and walk to the mushroom safespot; if prayer runs low, teleport immediately.

Escape crystal: you may carry it set to a short inactivity timer, but nothing here credits it. Its behaviour in open-world Isafdar is undocumented and it never fires while you move. Never lower any other precaution because of it.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: Tirannwn is the first link of the long Song of the Elves chain toward Prifddinas, out of reach today but worth keeping in mind.
Safer choice: decision point `DP02` option A, at the cost of this reward and the Tirannwn gate.

steps.summary: Danger first: Koschei's first three forms are run-ending on Hardcore Worlds and have no documented exit; only his fourth form is a safe death. In return you get {{step.xp_gained}} Agility XP, the quest Defence your zerker plan wants, and the enchanted lyre that makes Rellekka practical.
instructions: Bank for the road trips: food, Camelot teleport tablets (at least two per trip), and Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.

Travel before you have the lyre: Camelot tablet, then the road north, keeping left at the first fork. Stay on the road, do not attempt the log balance north of Sinclair Mansion, and do not fight anything on the road.
Do: farm the lyre from the non-aggressive citizens, using the fire safespots with Ranged.
Do: fight the Draugen only during the hunt, at full HP with food.

Bank before the Koschei duel: BANK your escape crystal, take off and bank any ring of life, withdraw a full inventory of the best food you can buy (monkfish, {{fact:F-4062}} each, is the largest verified heal) and an antipoison. Leave weapons, armour and runes behind: they are not allowed in the duel.
Before the duel: cure any poison, check your connection is stable, and be at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}).
Do, first three forms: start every form at full HP, eat at the card's eat line, and trap Koschei across the floor hole or by the fire pillars to eat and regenerate.
Do, fourth form: do not resist. Let him wear you down until the fight ends on its own; this form is the safe phase.
Stop: when the quest completes. Keep the enchanted lyre charged for Rellekka.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}): the highest with-prep score on the Balanced route. In the first three forms there is no documented exit and a death is run-ending; a disconnect in the second or third form is likely fatal, and no verified mitigation covers it. Your only controls are food, full HP before each form, trapping him, and a stable connection.

BANK THE ESCAPE CRYSTAL before the Koschei duel. Worn, it acts like a ring of life and resets the fight to the first form. Carried in your inventory, it can fire if you stand still in the fourth form while he hits you, which also throws you out and resets the fight. Either way you are sent back through the run-ending first three forms, and nothing in the duel credits the crystal, so leave it in the bank.

NEVER wear a ring of life in the Koschei duel. It sends you to your respawn point and restarts the fight at the first form; worn into the fourth form it would reset the fight every time, so the quest could never be finished. It is not an exit.
Mandatory: start every form at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}), eat at the card's eat line, and trap Koschei across the floor hole or by the fire pillars whenever you need to eat and regenerate.

Stop condition: in the first three forms, if your food falls to the card's reserve line, trap Koschei and stall. After long enough in one phase he disappears and the fight restarts at the first form: a time cost, not a death. Then leave between fights the normal way and restock. Try walking or teleporting out only as a last resort; neither is documented.
Mandatory: start the duel only on a stable connection and never below full HP. A disconnect leaves you in combat for up to a minute. Stop on any unstable connection before the duel.

Camelot road, first trips before the lyre: travel at full HP with food and your Camelot tablets. Never fight on the road: walk on through chip damage, but teleport away at once if HP falls to the card's road line or two attackers engage, and report what attacked you. The road's monsters and the log balance's fail damage are unresearched.

If the Draugen engages outside the hunt (it is aggressive and roams the province), teleport away rather than fight it unprepared. Stop condition: leave Rellekka if HP falls to the card's Draugen line during the fight.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event during the quest; never accept one on the road or in the province.

This card has changed since you first accepted this step: the ring of life is gone from it, there is no exit in the first three forms, and the early trips use an unresearched road. Read it again before you take decision point `DP08` option B.
tips: Why it is worth it: Agility XP, quest Defence that stays far under your cap (watch the cap bar on the Balanced route), and the lyre teleport that removes the long Camelot road from Rellekka.
Safer alternative: decision point `DP08` option A, staying on Pollnivneach with no Fremennik Trials.

steps.summary: Danger first: several aggressive Troll generals hit hard enough that two hits kill you from full HP, and once you are low a single hit can. The prep card brings it down to {{risk.tier}}, for {{fact:F-2022}} and the gate to Troll Romance.
instructions: Bank: a full inventory of monkfish ({{fact:F-4062}} each, the largest verified heal), prayer potions, a games necklace, and Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: Trollheim by the rock shortcuts, which avoid the thrower trolls on the mountain path.
Do: fight Dad only from the western-gate safespot, with Ranged.
Do: turn Protect from Melee on before entering the generals' room, then kill only the southern-most general from the desk safespot with Ranged.
Do: fight Berry and Twig only from inside a vacant cell.
Do: leave by the secret exit to the south and teleport out.
Stop: at quest completion, or at any stop condition below.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}} (Extreme, with the very top of the game ladder), with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}). Why you might still do it: a quest completion and the gate to Troll Romance. For Agility alone it is optional; decision point `DP03` option A skips it.
Mandatory: never enter the generals' room without Protect from Melee on, full prayer and full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}).
Mandatory: in the generals' room, eat whenever your HP is at or below a general's maximum hit (the card's eat line). Below it, one hit can kill you.
Stop conditions: leave if two generals are attacking; leave the room and teleport if food or prayer falls to the card's lines.
Never fight a general in melee range. Bail-out: keep Protect from Melee on, back away to the desk safespot or out of the room, and teleport.
Escape crystal: optional and not credited. Its scope here is undocumented and it does not fire while you move; never lower another precaution because of it.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: If you also plan Troll Romance (`DP03` option C), do this first: it tests whether you can hold a protection prayer and eat under fire before Arrg.

steps.summary: Danger first: Arrg attacks the moment you arrive, and the run to the safespot cannot be made fully safe, even with perfect preparation. The reward is an Agility reward of {{fact:F-2031}}, which saves almost no training time.
instructions: Bank: a full inventory of monkfish ({{fact:F-4062}} each), leaving room for prayer potions; Ranged weapon and ammunition.
Gear: Ranged on Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange: Longrange (like any defensive style) gives Defence XP and breaks your zerker rule of quest-only Defence.
Travel: Trollheim to the troll arena at full HP and full prayer, on a stable connection.
Do: turn Protect from Melee on before you talk to Arrg.

Do: run straight to the north-west wall / west-gate safespot without stopping to fight. Eat one piece at once whenever HP reaches the card's run eat line (that is, after almost any hit) and keep moving.
Do: at the safespot, switch to Protect from Missiles and fight with Ranged. Eat at the card's safespot eat line and keep prayer topped up with prayer potions.
Stop: when Arrg dies, or hold the safespot until he despawns if a stop condition is met.
warnings: THE RUN TO THE SAFESPOT CANNOT BE MADE FULLY SAFE. This is the honest limit of the card: with Protect from Melee on, two maximum ranged hits with one monkfish between them leave you almost dead from full HP, and a third hit before the safespot, or any melee hit that slips through the prayer after the first, kills you. No verified food heals more, no combo-eating is verified, and the run's length is not documented. Surviving it depends on Arrg's hit rolls.

Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}): the highest with-prep score of any step in this plan. A death here is run-ending; the wiki says it is not a safe death even for Hardcore Ironmen.

Stop conditions before you start: do not start unless you accept that the run can kill a correctly prepared player, and do not start if Troll Stronghold showed you cannot hold a protection prayer and eat under fire.
Mandatory: talk to Arrg only at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}), full prayer, Protect from Melee already on and a full inventory of monkfish-class food.
Mandatory: start only on a stable connection. A disconnect leaves you in combat for up to a minute, and the run is the phase where both of his attacks can reach you.

Stop condition: if food or prayer falls to the card's lines at the safespot, stop attacking and hold the safespot under Protect from Missiles until Arrg despawns; then leave and come back fully stocked.

During the run there is no bail-out: keep moving and eat. Whether a teleport works in the arena is undocumented, so try one only as a last resort; logging out is not an exit under fire, and the escape crystal cannot cover the run because it never fires while you move.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: Why you might still do it: the Strength XP and the quest completion. For the Agility goal it is optional, and decision point `DP03` option A skips it.

steps.summary: No Agility XP: unlocks Herblore and leads to Recruitment Drive (decision point `DP04`, option B).
instructions: Bank: the raw meats for the cauldron, the card's food and a teleport.
Gear: light gear; you are running, not fighting.
Travel: Taverley, then Taverley Dungeon, at full HP.
Do: run past the skeletons and the suits of armour without fighting.
Stop: at quest completion; teleport out of the dungeon.
warnings: Mandatory: enter Taverley Dungeon at full HP with food, run past the skeletons and suits without fighting, and teleport out if HP falls to the card's line.
Stop condition: stop if more than two monsters follow you.
The dungeon monsters' max hits were not researched; the score is conservative for that reason.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.

steps.summary: No Agility XP: a Recruitment Drive prerequisite with two combat lamps, and Defence must never be chosen on either.
instructions: Bank: the quest disguise items, the card's food and a teleport.
Gear: the disguise; no fight is required.
Travel: the Black Knights' Fortress, north of Falador.
Do: evade the Black Knights; do not fight them.
Do: rub both lamps into Attack, Strength, Ranged, Magic, Hitpoints or Prayer.
Stop: at quest completion.
warnings: NEVER click Defence on either lamp. It is offered as a valid choice, and on your zerker build it is a trap.
Mandatory: evade the knights at full HP with food; leave and teleport if more than one engages or HP falls to the card's line.
The knights' max hit was not researched; the score is conservative for that reason.

steps.summary: An Agility reward of {{fact:F-2009}} after two prerequisite quests; the fight is against Sir Leye with no armour or food allowed.
instructions: Bank: nothing to bring; the tests do not allow armour, food or potions.
Travel: the Temple Knight testing grounds in Falador.
Do: work through the tests; fight Sir Leye at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}).
Stop: at quest completion, or by the yellow portal at any stop condition below.
warnings: Mandatory: leave by the yellow portal at the start of the room if HP falls to the card's line or Sir Leye is healing faster than you damage him.
This fight is not a safe death, even for Hardcore Ironmen; on Hardcore Worlds it is official.
tips: Three quests for a small Agility reward: only worth it if you are clearing quests for their own sake.

steps.summary: An Agility reward of {{fact:F-2501}}, but blocked by its Thieving requirement; its fights are scripted to stop before death.
instructions: First: train Thieving to the requirement shown on this step. That training is your choice and has not been danger-rated; ask for a rating before you pick a method.
Bank: nothing can be carried into the villa; the Head Butler holds your items.
Travel: Varlamore, Villa Lucens.
Do: enter the villa at full HP ({{risk.min_hitpoints}}) and fight the two scripted fights.
Stop: if a fight goes wrong, stop attacking and let the scripted fight end; walk out and reclaim your items from the Head Butler.
warnings: Mandatory: enter the villa at full HP. You go in with no food, equipment, escape crystal or teleports.
Stop condition: if Naiatli deals real damage beyond chip, stop and ask for a re-rating.
No Hardcore Worlds safe exception covers this quest: the wiki says the fights cannot kill, but any death that did happen would be official.
tips: Never drink a poison chalice for a Thieving boost: it can deal more damage than your whole HP.

steps.summary: Long-term goal only: locked behind Sins of the Father and a Hitpoints level well above yours. Danger first: trap damage is undocumented and a death here is ordinary and official.
instructions: Before you can start: complete Sins of the Father (its veto lifts only after its fights are researched and its prep card is written) and train Hitpoints to the wiki's recommendation ({{fact:F-3056}}).
Bank: food until you own the hallowed ring, antipoison, stamina potions and a Saradomin item.
Gear: the hallowed ring as soon as you can afford it, and a Saradomin item so the obelisks restore your run energy.
Travel: a hallowed crystal shard straight to the lobby, or vyre noble robes for Darkmeyer.
Do: practise the first three floors before the fourth ({{fact:F-0018}}).
Do: after a trap hit, stop on a tile clear of traps, eat to full, then move on.
Stop: at the card's floor HP line. The exit plan is 'stop, eat, then move', never 'teleport'.
warnings: Headline {{risk.inherent_ds}}, with prep {{risk.residual_ds}} ({{risk.tier}}), rated at your current Hitpoints. It will be re-rated at your stats when it becomes reachable.
Mandatory: do not enter below {{risk.min_hitpoints}} Hitpoints, the wiki's recommendation and the only verified guidance on trap damage. You must train Hitpoints first.
Mandatory: buy the hallowed ring first and wear it on every run; it negates trap damage (not portal-frame or grapple failures).
Mandatory: never cross Darkmeyer without vyre noble robes unless you arrive by crystal shard; the Vyrewatch Sentinels are aggressive otherwise.
Mandatory: carry antipoison for failed coffin loot, and carry stamina potions and wear a Saradomin item so you never stand still mid-floor without run energy.
Stop conditions: stop running floors if HP falls to the card's line and eat to full on a clear tile; stop and ask for a re-rating if a single trap hit deals more than the card's limit.
Defence cap: the Sins of the Father chain forces some Defence XP on you; with The Fremennik Trials it still stays under your cap. Put no lamp or tome from the chain into Defence.
The escape crystal's behaviour inside the Sepulchre is undocumented; never plan around it.
Stop condition: dismiss every random event here and never accept one. A death inside a random event is an official death on Hardcore Worlds.
tips: There are no marks of grace here ({{fact:F-1061}}); get your Graceful on the rooftops first.

steps.summary: Stay-on-Seers' option for the next band (decision point `DP06`, option B): a familiar course with the bank at the start, but slower than Pollnivneach and failing until {{fact:F-1018}}.
instructions: Bank: Seers' Village bank at the start; take the card's food (you need less once fails stop).
Gear: Graceful or light clothing.
Travel: walk from the bank; Camelot tablets land at Camelot.
Do: run laps with Rapid Heal on; recharge at the church altar; buy food at the Forester's Arms.
Do: eat whenever HP is {{risk.min_hitpoints}} or lower.
Stop: at {{fact:F-1033}}, when Rellekka opens.
warnings: Fail damage here is not published, so the card uses a conservative rule (not a sourced bound): eat whenever HP is {{risk.min_hitpoints}} or lower, never attempt a failable obstacle below the card's stop line, and stop and ask for a re-rating after any single fail bigger than the card's limit. The exact lines are in 'Stop immediately if' on this step's danger card. The failable obstacles are the first gap and the tightrope.
Dismiss every random event and never accept one mid-lap: a death inside one is official on Hardcore Worlds. Never go AFK; break sessions into blocks of an hour or less.
tips: Pollnivneach (the recommended option) is faster and its fail damage is small and known.

outro:
When the last Ardougne lap lands, you will have earned that cape the hard way, one life and all.

Two longer roads stay on the map, and neither is closed because it is too dangerous. Both are blocked by missing facts, and each one says what lifts it.

Werewolf Agility Course (with Creature of Fenkenstrain, which only unlocks it): blocked because the deathslide's maximum fall damage is unpublished. A fall can hit very hard, does not scale with Hitpoints and can exceed your current HP, so nobody can tell you at what HP a fall is survivable. It lifts when EITHER your Agility and Strength both pass the deathslide's published never-fail point while you carry almost nothing (the Risk Officer sets the bar just above that point), OR a source publishes the deathslide maximum and the Risk Officer re-rates the course with a minimum-HP rule above it. Then both steps return and the calculator re-runs.

Sins of the Father, and through it the Hallowed Sepulchre: blocked because the quest's fights were never researched for max hits and teleport or instance rules, and the final boss's maximum is disputed, so no bail-out can be written from verified facts. It lifts when, as you near its skill and quest requirements, a research request covers those fights and the Risk Officer completes its prep card and re-rates it at your stats at that time. Its tome can then go straight into Agility. The Sepulchre also wants far more Hitpoints than you have today, and the chain's forced Defence still fits under your cap. The exact requirements are listed with the plan's assumptions.

The Graveyard and its new course are announced but not released, so they are not in this guide; if you ever take its lamps, never choose Defence. Until next time: carpets, not legs; prayer up before the fight, not during it; and when the card says stop, stop. Safe running, adventurer.

Read schemas/prose.schema.json, tools/validate.py g_prose (bare-number scan, token grammar, fact usability), tools/assemble.py (which facts reach the guide) and templates/guide.html tokens()/stepCard()/pRoute() (how prose and tokens render).

Generated prose.json with a local script (scratchpad build_prose.py) that also self-checks: no digits outside tokens/backticks, token grammar, fact usability and presence in the shipped fact set, no step tokens on off-route steps, no tokens in intro/outro.

decisions.decision: Intro and outro contain no tokens and no digits.
decisions.reason: templates/guide.html renders intro/outro with esc() only (no token resolution), so a token there would print raw braces; the validator also bans digits there.
alternatives_considered: Put score tokens in the intro (would render as raw {{...}})

decisions.decision: The Fractured Archive anchor is described as 'the very top of the scale' instead of quoting its number.
decisions.reason: No token carries the ladder anchor and a bare digit is banned; the guide's danger badge tooltip and Danger tab print 'The Fractured Archive = 100' from the template.
alternatives_considered: Spell the number out in words (would sidestep the no-bare-numbers rule)

decisions.decision: HP thresholds that have no token (eat lines, stop lines, re-rating limits, food reserves) are named by role and pointed to the card ('the card's eat line', 'Stop immediately if'); {{risk.min_hitpoints}} is used wherever the card's minimum HP equals the rule being stated.
decisions.reason: Only {{risk.min_hitpoints}} exposes an HP number; the danger card printed directly below the prose shows every exact threshold from risk.json. Borrowing an unrelated fact whose value happens to match (e.g. a food heal) would mislabel the source.

decisions.decision: Small counts and ordinals copied from risk.json (two attackers, three monsters, the first three forms, the fourth form, both lamps) are written in words.
decisions.reason: They label phases and counts stated in the sealed risk card, not quantities from calc or facts; digits are banned and no token exists for them.

decisions.decision: {{step.*}} tokens only on route steps (S01-S06, S08-S14); off-route steps (S07, S15-S21, S25, S26) use fact tokens for rewards and levels.
decisions.reason: tokens() resolves step.* against the selected route's calc; steps outside every route have no calc row and would print a dash.

decisions.decision: RT-16 handled in S12: bank the escape crystal before the duel, never wear a ring of life; the risk card's optional 'carry it in the inventory' line is superseded in the prose by the dispatch's instruction, with the reason stated.
decisions.reason: Dispatch requires it; the crystal earns no credit in the duel and carrying it can reset the fight in the fourth form (F-3017/F-3018/F-5009/F-5011/F-0015).

decisions.decision: S17 leads with 'THE RUN TO THE SAFESPOT CANNOT BE MADE FULLY SAFE' and paraphrases S17-M4 without numbers.
decisions.reason: Dispatch and the Risk Officer's 'print it in the guide' instruction.

decisions.decision: Q-01 and Q-02 disclosed in the intro; Balanced is justified by lyre, Tirannwn and quest Defence, never by time.
Q-03 disclosed as an S09 tip ('may run a couple of hours longer').
decisions.reason: Quant recommendation; exact figure has no token.

decisions.decision: Decision-point IDs (e.g. `DP03`) are written in backticks.
decisions.reason: They are identifiers that contain digits, like item names; the guide's Decisions tab and 'What next?' panel show the same IDs, so the reader can find them.
alternatives_considered: Describe each decision point by its question only (harder to cross-reference)

decisions.decision: Every Ranged fight step tells the owner to use Rapid or Accurate, never Longrange.
decisions.reason: brief.json build xp_rules forbid combat styles that give Defence XP.

decisions.decision: Steps with a residual tier of Moderate or above (S01, S12, S16, S17, S25) open their summary with 'Danger first'.
decisions.reason: Charter: begin such steps with their warning; the template prints warnings after the instructions, so the summary carries the lead.

limitations: Exact eat lines, stop lines, food reserves and re-rating limits are not repeated as numbers in the prose (no token exists); the reader must use the danger card printed under each step, which the template always renders from risk.json.
The ladder anchor value (The Fractured Archive = 100) is not stated as a number in the prose; it appears in the template's badge tooltip and Danger tab.
Prose for off-route steps (S07, S15-S21, S25, S26) is written and validated but the current template only renders prose for steps on the selected route.

RT-16 remains open in redteam.json; the prose tells the owner to bank the crystal, but the risk card's optional S12-M6 still says it may be carried in the inventory. The Risk Officer should align the card.
RT-17 (CLI/doc labelling of headline vs raw) is open; the prose uses 'headline' and 'with prep' per docs/05 and the policy.
Fact tokens with dictionary values render poorly, so only scalar or short-string facts are tokenised.
